title: Add editor setting for 3D Freelook global Y vertical movement
body:
### Problem
When navigating the 3D editor viewport in Free Look / Fly mode with the default navigation scheme (`FREELOOK_DEFAULT`), pressing `E` (up) or `Q` (down) while looking downward caused the camera to drift diagonally forward/backward due to the `up` vector being calculated from the camera's local pitch orientation.

### Solution
- Added a new Editor Setting `editors/3d/freelook/freelook_vertical_movement_global` (enabled by default).
- When enabled (`true`), Free Look vertical motion keys (`E` and `Q`) move strictly along the global world Y axis (`Vector3(0, 1, 0)`), preventing unintended horizontal drift regardless of camera pitch angle.
- When disabled (`false`), behavior falls back to camera-relative pitch orientation in the Default navigation scheme.
- Forward/backward and strafe keys (`W`, `A`, `S`, `D`) remain camera-oriented.
- Added automated unit tests in `tests/scene/test_view_3d_controller.cpp` verifying pitch independence, zero horizontal drift, and toggling of the setting.

### How to test
1. Open the 3D editor viewport.
2. In Free Look mode (holding Right Mouse Button), tilt the camera downwards and press `E` or `Q`.
3. Verify that vertical elevation occurs purely along the world vertical axis with zero forward/backward drift.
4. Go to **Editor Settings > Editors > 3D > Freelook**, disable `Freelook Vertical Movement Global`, and verify that movement behaves relative to camera pitch.
5. Run unit tests via `./bin/godot.windows.editor.x86_64.console.exe --test --test-case="*[View3DController]*"`.
